tagline: Through Cow Creek Canyon with the railroad, and a gold pan.
intro: Off I-5 at Riddle, Cow Creek Road heads west, and the farms and ranches give way to deep forest in Cow Creek Canyon. Road and creek run together most of the way, and the railroad that shares the canyon still follows the Oregon and California grade of 1869.

Past the West Fork of Cow Creek the road crosses two steel girder bridges built in 1905. Beyond Skull Creek Campground it rises out of the forest into pasture and orchards and comes back to I-5 at Glendale.
season: TripCheck gives spring for waterfalls and wildflowers and fall for color as the best times.

moments.title: Riddle
moments.text: Named for a pioneer of 1851, Riddle had the last nickel mine and smelter to operate in the lower 48, until the mine closed in 1987.

moments.title: Island Creek Day Use Area
moments.text: A creekside stop to stretch the legs, picnic, or try a gold pan in Cow Creek, while minding the private mining claims marked along the banks.

moments.title: Glendale
moments.text: The railroad's right-of-way agent named it Julia, after his wife, but after a dispute the chief engineer renamed it Glendale, and the Julia post office lasted from February to August 1883.

practical: Paved and open all year, with no services between Riddle and the end of the route and logging trucks common on the blind corners.

sources.label: Bureau of Land Management, Cow Creek Back Country Byway
